content.text:
I submitted index 20 (Co 0.33 / Sb 0.67, the CoSb₂O₆ composition) as the best composition. It had the highest EQE of the three I measured, but that is only 0.055%, so this is a weak result overall. All 3 merit measurements are used; none of the 5 XRD measurements were used.

| Index | Composition (Co/Sb) | Expected phase | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **20** | 0.33 / 0.67 | CoSb₂O₆ (rutile-type) | **0.055** |
| 5 | 0.79 / 0.21 | Co₇Sb₂O₁₂ (spinel) | 0.0035 |
| 24 | 0.23 / 0.77 | CoSb₂O₆ plus extra Sb oxide | 0.0027 |

- **Why index 20 first:** the stability model (MACE) puts CoSb₂O₆ exactly on the stability limit (0 eV/atom above the hull), so that composition should form a single clean phase.
- **Band-gap predictions were not useful:** the band-gap model (MEGNet) gave 0.37 eV for CoSb₂O₆, 1.44 eV for the spinel and 1.93 eV for CoSb₂O₄. The 0.37 eV figure is almost certainly too low for this kind of cobalt oxide, and none of the three values matched the ranking I measured.
- **What the ranking suggests:** both points either side of index 20 came in about 15–20× lower. That suggests merit peaks at the CoSb₂O₆ composition, but three points can't confirm it.

Most of the library is unmeasured, including the whole region between indices 5 and 20 (Sb 0.24–0.64). With only three points, a better composition could exist in that gap or right next to index 20.
